strapline: Twenty-four ministers sworn in, the budget slips to 6 November, K14.6 billion owed for maize, and the under-15s beat England

stories.title: Twenty-four ministers in an afternoon: Hichilema fills the 30-ministry Cabinet, gives Tambatamba the mines and splits Energy between Kapala and Chikote
stories.excerpt: A day after Parliament approved the new structure, President Hakainde Hichilema swore in 24 Cabinet ministers at State House on Wednesday 28 October, filling the posts left empty since August. Brenda Tambatamba moves from Labour to Mines, Peter Kapala and Makozo Chikote take the new Electricity and Petroleum ministries, Felix Mutati and Douglas Syakalima return, and Jack Mwiimbu moves from Home Affairs to Justice. Fred M'membe called the expansion out of touch; Highvie Hamududu called its cost insignificant.

image.label: The full front bench
image.caption: President Hichilema swore in 24 Cabinet ministers and ten provincial ministers at State House in Lusaka on Wednesday 28 October 2026, completing a government of 30 ministries.

body: The Cabinet of four is over. President Hakainde Hichilema appointed and swore in 24 Cabinet ministers at State House on Wednesday 28 October, Zambia Monitor and Open Zambia reported, a day after the National Assembly adopted the Vice-President's motion creating a government of 30 ministries. Anadolu Agency reported that all ten provincial ministers were sworn in at the same ceremony. Reuters, in a report carried by CNBC Africa, described the appointments as cabinet changes following the President's re-election in August.

The 24 join the four ministers appointed in September: Anadolu Agency lists their portfolios as Health, Finance and National Planning, Green Economy and Environment, and Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. Situmbeko Musokotwane holds Finance and has been acting at Agriculture; Mulambo Haimbe, the Foreign Affairs Minister, was in Moscow on Wednesday for the Russia-Africa Summit.

Zambia Monitor's list runs as follows. Ambrose Lufuma stays at Defence. Clement Andeleki takes Home Affairs and Internal Security, the post Jack Mwiimbu held in the first term; Mwiimbu moves to Justice. Moses Moyo, the former Second Deputy Speaker, takes Agriculture, and Olive Chiboola, elected in August for the new Namwala East constituency, takes Fisheries and Livestock. Caroline Katotobwe, a policy and governance specialist from civil society, takes the new Ministry of Trade and Exports; Noel Nkoma, an economist and former chairman of the National Road Fund Agency board, takes Industry; Lucky Sichone, the Konkola MP and former Mayor of Chililabombwe, takes Small and Medium Enterprise Development.

Brenda Tambatamba, Labour Minister since 2021 and before politics a sustainability manager at Barrick's Lumwana mine, becomes Minister of Mines and Minerals Development; Anadolu Agency says she is the first woman to hold the post. The old Ministry of Energy goes to two former energy ministers: Peter Kapala takes Electricity and Makozo Chikote takes Petroleum. Princess Kasune moves from Justice to Tourism, Collins Nzovu from Water to Infrastructure and Urban Development, Patrick Mucheleka takes Lands and Elisha Matambo, the former Copperbelt provincial minister, takes Water Development and Sanitation.

Elvis Nkandu, the former Youth, Sport and Arts Minister, becomes Minister of Information and Media and chief government spokesperson. Harry Kamboni, the Kalomo Central MP and former chair of Parliament's education committee, takes Education, and Douglas Syakalima, nominated to Parliament and sworn in as an MP on Tuesday, News Diggers reported, takes the new Ministry of Skills and Higher Education; Felix Mutati, nominated the same day, returns to Technology and Science and Gift Sialubalo returns to Local Government and Rural Development. Misheck Nyambose takes Labour and Social Security, Sheal Mulyata takes Community Development and Social Services, Likando Mufalali takes Youth and Sports, and Christopher Chibuye, the Mkushi North MP and a former PF member, becomes the first Minister of Culture and Arts.

Zambia Monitor reported the President's remarks at the ceremony. He told the ministers to uphold the Constitution, respect the rule of law and serve every Zambian equally, and he warned that any minister who blocked or delayed investment would be treated as behaving badly in Cabinet. Where a law stood in the government's way, he said, it should be changed through Parliament rather than broken.

body.text: We stay within the law. We operate within the law.
body.attribution: President Hakainde Hichilema at the swearing-in at State House on Wednesday 28 October, as reported by Zambia Monitor

body: He directed that beneficiaries of the Social Cash Transfer, FISP and the Food Security Pack be chosen on eligibility alone, with no distinction by where people live, and said he had confronted those responsible for distortions in how social support was distributed. He described the government as starting from a "zero base" and said incentives could be granted to investors because Pay As You Earn alone would lift revenue. Anadolu Agency quoted a State House post after the ceremony: "As a government, we have a duty and a responsibility to deliver equitable development to all our people."

The appointments came as the argument over 30 ministries continued. News Diggers reported on Wednesday that Socialist Party president Fred M'membe called the expansion proof that the administration was "out of touch" with the hardship facing ordinary Zambians, saying the country needed a "lean and efficient administration" rather than a "bloated government" and could be run with at most ten Cabinet portfolios. In the same report, Highvie Hamududu, the leader of the Party of National Unity and Progress, defended the expansion and called the additional cost "insignificant". The Zambia Daily Mail reported that the Vice-President, moving Tuesday's motion, argued that electricity needed a ministry of its own to look for new ways to generate, transmit and supply power, and that culture and arts should be treated as an economic opportunity.

The documents before Parliament, as Open Zambia's account of the appendix noted and as Lusaka Brief reported on Tuesday and Wednesday, carry no cost estimate for the additional ministries. Citizens First had asked on Tuesday for the budget to be postponed until a full Cabinet was in place, and the Vice-President told Parliament the same day that the presentation would move from Friday 30 October to Friday 6 November, News Diggers reported; that story is covered separately in this edition.

body.confirmed: Twenty-four Cabinet ministers were sworn in at State House on Wednesday 28 October (Zambia Monitor; Open Zambia; Reuters via CNBC Africa), with ten provincial ministers (Anadolu Agency). Tambatamba holds Mines, Kapala Electricity, Chikote Petroleum, Mwiimbu Justice, Andeleki Home Affairs, Nkandu Information and Media, Mutati Technology and Science and Sialubalo Local Government: all the outlets read for this edition agree on these.
body.unverified: Education and Skills and Higher Education: Zambia Monitor gives Syakalima the Skills and Higher Education ministry and Kamboni Education; Open Zambia lists them the other way round. The names of the ten provincial ministers, which no established outlet read for this edition carried. Lusaka Times reported reaction from Laura Miti and opposition leaders, but its page could not be opened. The cost of the enlarged Cabinet, which no published document states.

stories.title: A week's grace for the new ministers: the 2027 budget moves from Friday to 6 November, and the Vice-President says the government is 'still working on it'
stories.excerpt: Vice-President Mutale Nalumango told Parliament on Tuesday 27 October that Situmbeko Musokotwane will now present the 2027 national budget on Friday 6 November rather than 30 October, News Diggers reports. The change came the day before 24 ministers were sworn in, and after Citizens First argued that ministers appointed on a Wednesday could not defend a budget on the Friday. ZIPAR, meanwhile, has asked the Treasury not to cut PAYE.

image.label: 6 November
image.caption: The presentation of Zambia's 2027 national budget has been moved from Friday 30 October to Friday 6 November 2026, according to a statement to Parliament by the Vice-President.

body: The budget will not be read on Friday. News Diggers reported on Wednesday 28 October that Vice-President Mutale Nalumango told the National Assembly the presentation of the 2027 national budget had been moved from 30 October to 6 November, saying the government was "still working on it". The report says she made the announcement on Tuesday while winding up debate on the motion to dissolve, realign and create ministries, after Shiwang'andu MP Stephen Kampyongo raised the budget during the debate. The rest of the report sits behind the paper's paywall and could not be read in full.

Only four days earlier the timetable had looked settled. In her business statement on Friday 24 October, reported by News Diggers the same day, the Vice-President said the Minister of Finance and National Planning, Situmbeko Musokotwane, would present the budget on Friday 30 October; that the Speaker, Nelly Mutti, would within seven days suspend the business of the House for ten working days of sector budget analysis; and that business would resume on 24 November. She also said she would move a motion on Thursday 29 October to suspend Standing Order 25 so the House could sit from 14:15 on the Friday until the budget business was concluded. With the presentation moved a week, the suspension and the 24 November resumption will presumably shift too, though no outlet read for this edition had reported the revised calendar.

The postponement follows, though no report links the two, a call from Citizens First. The Zambian Observer reported on Tuesday 27 October that the party's spokesperson, Stanley Mhango, had asked the President to postpone the presentation and appoint a full Cabinet first, or else to explain how the government would proceed without ministerial input. He argued that the budget had been put together without line ministers and that a Cabinet named days before the reading could not have taken part in a process that was already closed.

body.text: A minister cannot reasonably be appointed on Wednesday to defend a budget he or she has never seen on Friday.
body.attribution: Stanley Mhango, Citizens First spokesperson, in a statement reported by the Zambian Observer on Tuesday 27 October

body: Mhango cited Article 116 of the Constitution on collective responsibility and said that while the budget might still pass, a document without ministerial input raised what he called authenticity concerns about public buy-in and ownership of its implementation. As it turned out, the ministers were sworn in on Wednesday and the budget will be read eight days later.

body.text: What the Treasury is being asked to do

body: The week's delay gives the lobbying a little longer to run. The Zambia Institute for Policy Analysis and Research told a press briefing on Monday, News Diggers reported on Tuesday, that the government should not reduce the Pay As You Earn rate in the 2027 budget because the Grow Zambia Agenda needs more revenue, not less. ZIPAR's executive director, Zali Chikuba, also said the institute expected faster progress on open access to the TAZAMA pipeline, which it argues would bring efficiency and transparency to the oil marketing sector, and he defended the Ministry of Finance's two supplementary budgets in one year as a response to information the government did not have when it planned, rather than poor planning.

That position sits awkwardly with what the President told his new ministers on Wednesday. Zambia Monitor reported him saying the government was in a "zero base" situation and that incentives could be granted to investors because PAYE alone would improve revenue. Whether the budget cuts the rate, leaves it alone or widens the base will be known on 6 November.

stories.title: K4.1 billion paid, K14.6 billion still owed: Musokotwane says most maize farmers will be paid in November once the Treasury releases K14.7 billion, and the FRA has export contracts
stories.excerpt: In a ministerial statement on Tuesday 27 October the acting Agriculture Minister said the Food Reserve Agency had bought 2.7 million tonnes of maize worth K18.738 billion from 1,850 depots this season, far above its 500,000-tonne target, and had so far paid K4.1 billion of it. The balance is to come from the supplementary budget, with most payments expected next month, Zambia Monitor and the Zambia Daily Mail report.

image.label: The FRA ledger
image.caption: The Food Reserve Agency bought 2.7 million tonnes of maize in the 2025/26 marketing season and still owed farmers about K14.6 billion at the end of October 2026, Parliament was told.

body: Farmers who sold their maize to the Food Reserve Agency this season are owed about K14.6 billion, and most of them should be paid in November. That was the message Situmbeko Musokotwane, the Finance Minister acting at Agriculture, gave the National Assembly in a ministerial statement on Tuesday 27 October, reported by Zambia Monitor on Tuesday and the Zambia Daily Mail on Wednesday. News Diggers carried the same figure under the headline "Govt owes maize farmers K14.6bn".

The numbers, as both outlets report them, are these. The FRA opened crop buying on 29 July with a target of 500,000 tonnes of maize and 1,000 tonnes of paddy rice. Farmers offered so much grain that the maize target was raised to 2.7 million tonnes, and the agency bought that amount from 1,850 buying depots at a cost of K18.738 billion. It also bought 1,304.41 tonnes of rice worth K9.7 million. Of the maize bill, K4.1 billion has been paid.

body.text: a sum of K4.1 billion has since been paid to farmers for maize already delivered to the agency
body.attribution: Situmbeko Musokotwane, acting Minister of Agriculture, in a ministerial statement to Parliament on Tuesday 27 October, as reported by Zambia Monitor

body: The Treasury is to provide K14.7 billion through the 2026 supplementary budget to clear the arrears, and the ministry aims to make most of the payments by November. Musokotwane said the government remained committed to settling every outstanding payment as funds became available and thanked farmers for their patience. The Daily Mail's report gives the outstanding balance as K14.6 billion in one place and K14.7 billion in another; the K14.7 billion is the Treasury release, the K14.6 billion the debt it is meant to clear.

The statement also set out the size of the stockpile. Zambia produced an estimated 5.1 million tonnes of maize this year including seed maize, Zambia Monitor reports; with 1.42 million tonnes carried over, total stocks stood at 6.71 million tonnes against a national requirement of 4.2 million, leaving a marketable surplus of 2.5 million tonnes. The FRA's own stocks are expected to reach 4.1 million tonnes, the 1.42 million carried over plus this season's 2.7 million.

The agency has secured sales contracts for 1.7 million tonnes, 1.5 million of them for export and 212,000 for the domestic market, and the minister said export revenue would help sustain the strategic reserve and fund future purchases. He told the House that the reserve held enough maize to meet national needs until the next harvest, the Daily Mail reports, and that strengthening food security was a priority given the concern over El Niño.

The statement answers, in part, a question raised when the K19.9 billion supplementary budget was presented: how the Treasury would find the money for grain the FRA had not planned to buy. The answer given on Tuesday is that the money comes first and the export receipts follow. Whether the November payments arrive on the timetable the minister gave is the thing to watch.

stories.title: US$1.8 billion of suspected illicit flows, 580 tax cases and a shell company that turned K85 million into a K150 million contract: what the FIC's 2025 trends report says
stories.excerpt: The Financial Intelligence Centre's eleventh money laundering trends report puts suspected illicit financial flows at US$1.8 billion in 2025, down from US$3.5 billion in 2024, with 786 intelligence reports passed to law enforcement, most of them over suspected tax evasion by shell companies. Zambia Monitor and News Diggers report that ZRA assessments arising from the Centre's work exceeded K12.5 billion.

image.label: The 2025 trends report
image.caption: The Financial Intelligence Centre's trends report for 2025 records 786 intelligence reports disseminated, 580 of them over suspected tax evasion, and suspected illicit flows of US$1.8 billion.

body: The Financial Intelligence Centre detected US$1.8 billion in suspected illicit financial flows in 2025, down from US$3.5 billion the year before, according to its eleventh Money Laundering Trends Report, reported by News Diggers on Tuesday 27 October and in more detail by Zambia Monitor on Wednesday 28 October. The Centre disseminated 786 intelligence reports to law enforcement during the year, 17.4 per cent fewer than the 951 of 2024.

Tax crime dominates the ledger. Of the 786 reports, 580 concerned suspected tax evasion, 192 money laundering and 12 other offences such as corruption and fraud. The Centre says the suspected tax crimes were largely linked to shell companies that received funds through local and international transfers or large cash deposits by foreign nationals, after which the money was withdrawn in cash or sent to Asia on the pretext of importing goods. The Centre received 6,136 suspicious transaction reports in 2025, News Diggers reports.

Zambia Monitor sets out one case study from the report. A company it calls Company A received K85 million between October 2024 and July 2025 and passed about K70 million of it to Company B, which went on to win public contracts including a vehicle supply contract worth about K150 million. The report describes Company B as primarily a shell company used to obtain a public contract. The report does not name either company, and no charges arising from the case are reported.

On corruption, the Centre's 2025 National Risk Assessment rates the threat of corruption-related money laundering as medium-high, down from very high, and the Centre disseminated six corruption cases in 2025 against ten in 2024. The report nonetheless says corruption "remains a significant financial crime threat", with effects on public finances and governance and a distorting effect on procurement. Nineteen reports concerned environmental crime, chiefly illegal timber and ivory trafficking. Only three fraud cases were disseminated, a figure the Centre itself says does not reflect the scale of the threat the risk assessment identified.

The outcomes the report records are mostly on the tax side. The Zambia Revenue Authority raised assessments of more than K12.5 billion, including penalties and interest, on the back of the Centre's intelligence, Zambia Monitor reports; News Diggers gives the amount actually recovered by ZRA as more than K36.3 million. Law enforcement secured eight convictions, leading to the forfeiture of assets worth US$3.3 million, and advance income tax on remittances came to K485.1 million.

The fall in the headline figure, from US$3.5 billion to US$1.8 billion, is presented by both outlets as a decline in flows detected, not necessarily in flows that occurred; the report's own note that fraud is under-reported is a reminder of the difference. The Centre's reports are intelligence, not findings of guilt, and the cases it describes become public only if and when the agencies that receive them bring charges.

stories.title: 'We are around US$20 billion plus': Hichilema asks a Swiss trade mission to invest beyond copper and in joint ventures with Zambians, and thanks Bern for its part in the debt deal
stories.excerpt: A Swiss business delegation led by State Secretary Helene Artieda called at State House on Tuesday 27 October. The President urged investment beyond traditional minerals and said foreign investors should partner local businesses, arguing that joint ownership protects against expropriation; Artieda said Switzerland backs the Grow Zambia Agenda and is exploring a government-to-government platform for Swiss companies, the Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report.

image.label: Bern at State House
image.caption: A Swiss economic mission led by State Secretary Helene Artieda met President Hichilema at State House in Lusaka on Tuesday 27 October 2026.

body: President Hakainde Hichilema used a call from a Swiss economic mission on Tuesday 27 October to set out how he wants foreign investment to arrive in his second term: beyond copper, in partnership with Zambian businesses, and within a formal economic framework between the two countries. The delegation was led by Helene Artieda, State Secretary and Director of Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, the Zambia Daily Mail reported on Wednesday.

The President urged Switzerland to increase investment and trade beyond traditional minerals such as copper, to speed growth, create jobs and promote local value addition, and he called for a comprehensive economic partnership framework. He said trade between the two countries had grown over the years and that some Swiss investors had been in Zambia for some time.

body.text: Trade has evolved over the years, we are around US$20 billion plus.
body.attribution: President Hakainde Hichilema to the Swiss delegation at State House on Tuesday 27 October, as reported by the Zambia Daily Mail

body: The figure is the President's; neither report says what it measures or over what period. He also thanked Switzerland for its support in Zambia's debt restructuring, saying the country had moved from recovery and fiscal consolidation to accelerated growth, and that his second-term focus was growth through investment and trade with natural resources processed at home.

News Diggers reported the same meeting with a different emphasis. The President said Zambia wanted to move away from the traditional model in which European companies invest in Africa on their own, and that foreign investors should partner local businesses so that both sides benefit. Joint Zambian-foreign investments, he argued, would also protect investors against the possibility of expropriation, because citizens would hold a direct stake in the companies concerned.

Artieda said the Swiss government supported the Grow Zambia Agenda and would encourage Swiss businesses to take part in Zambia's economic goals, with interest in investment and cooperation in emerging sectors. News Diggers reported her saying Switzerland was exploring a government-to-government platform that would let Swiss companies increase their investments in Zambia. The Daily Mail reports that she supports the government's 10-10-5-3-3-1-1-1 growth targets, while adding that understanding the framework takes some effort.

The visit came a day before the President swore in his Cabinet, including a new Minister of Trade and Exports and a new Minister of Industry, portfolios created by the realignment that Parliament approved the same Tuesday. Whether the "comprehensive economic partnership framework" he asked for becomes a negotiated agreement is not something either report could say.

stories.title: A petition to scrap the two-term limit reaches Parliament through a UPND MP, Kabimba tells the President to silence those behind it, and the Attorney-General says time will tell
stories.excerpt: The Zambia Youth Organisation Consortium handed nominated MP Francis Kope a petition on Tuesday 27 October asking Parliament to abolish presidential term limits and drop the Grade 12 requirement for candidates; Kope said he would start the process of bringing it to the House, the Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report. Economic Front leader Wynter Kabimba said the President should tell those pushing a third term to 'shut up'.

image.label: Beyond 2031
image.caption: A youth consortium's petition asking Parliament to remove the presidential term limit was received by a UPND nominated MP at Parliament in Lusaka on Tuesday 27 October 2026.

body: The argument over whether President Hakainde Hichilema should be allowed to seek office after 2031 moved from radio studios to the steps of Parliament this week. On Tuesday 27 October a group calling itself the Zambia Youth Organisation Consortium presented a petition asking the National Assembly to abolish presidential term limits and to remove the Grade 12 certificate requirement for people seeking election as MPs and councillors, the Zambia Daily Mail reported on Wednesday. News Diggers reported that youth-led civil society organisations marched to Parliament to present it.

The consortium's chairperson, Jacob Longwe, argued that term limits restrict citizens' freedom to keep voting for the leaders they prefer and that the Grade 12 rule shuts out people with leadership qualities who lack the certificate. The Daily Mail names the member organisations as Youth for Dialogue, the Youth Development Network, Ambia Young Women, the Different Abled Youths Association and Arise and Soar Zambia, and says the group consulted around the country before drafting the petition. Neither report gives a number of signatures.

body.text: presidential term limits are not suitable in the current democratic dispensation
body.attribution: Jacob Longwe, chairperson of the Zambia Youth Organisation Consortium, at Parliament on Tuesday 27 October, as reported by the Zambia Daily Mail

body: The petition was received by Francis Kope, a UPND nominated MP, who was accompanied by Itezhi-tezhi West MP Twaambo Mutinta and Kaumbwe MP Charles Tembo. Kope promised to personally start the process of getting it presented to the House, and the consortium asked for it to be taken up as a private member's motion. Mutinta said a motion would let MPs debate the issues before any decision was taken.

Wynter Kabimba, the Economic Front leader, told Diamond TV's COSTA programme that the President should tell the people pushing to remove the term limit to "shut up", warning that the campaign would destroy him, News Diggers reported on Wednesday. He said he found it a pity that the debate had started barely two months after the UPND won an election; the rest of his remarks sit behind the paper's paywall.

The debate has been running inside the governing party since September. The Zambian Observer reported on 21 September that Florence Chama, a UPND proportional representation MP, had argued publicly that the President should remain in office beyond 2031, and that the Attorney-General, Mulilo Kabesha, had told Phoenix News that constitutional reform would follow lawful procedure and public participation and "will not be dictated by political commentary". On 6 October the Observer reported the UPND spokesperson, Cornelius Mweetwa, saying the party would not be held responsible for members calling for the limit to go, since they did not speak for it, and SACCORD's Arthur Muyunda warning that removing term limits would undermine the country's democratic gains.

Kabesha's most recent remarks are more open-ended. On the Zambia YMCA podcast, News Diggers reported on Monday 26 October, he said the government looked forward to possible constitutional amendments, that whether the term limit needed to go would be determined over time, and that if citizens demanded change the debate should not be suppressed. "Laws must be changing all the time, even if we claim or we like saying 'it should stand the test of time'," he said.

For now the position is this: the two-term limit stands in the Constitution, a petition to remove it has been handed to a governing-party MP who says he will bring it to the House, the party says the campaign is not its own, and the Attorney-General says the answer will come through the formal amendment process and the passage of time.

stories.title: Third time, still not started: the High Court orders Mukobeko to produce Mundubile, Zulu and 16 others at 10:00 on Thursday after the defence asks for time to answer the State
stories.excerpt: The constitutional bail application by Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused failed to get under way for a third time on Wednesday 28 October, Zambia Monitor reports. The defence asked for time to reply to the State's affidavit in opposition, served on Tuesday evening, and the applicants were again not brought from prison; the three-judge panel ordered them produced on Thursday morning and warned the officer in charge to appear and explain any failure.

image.label: Thursday, 10:00
image.caption: The Lusaka High Court ordered that Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused be brought from Mukobeko prison for their bail application on Thursday 29 October 2026.

body: The bail application that was due to resume on Wednesday 28 October did not start. Zambia Monitor reported that the hearing of the constitutional bail application by Brian Mundubile, the NRPUP presidential candidate in August's election, his running mate Makebi Zulu and 16 others failed to get under way for the third time, after the defence asked for more time to respond to the State's affidavit in opposition. The 18 are held at Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison and, as at the previous hearing, were not brought to court.

The panel of judges Derrick Mulenga, presiding, Davies Chibwili and Ireen Wishimanga ordered that all 18 applicants be brought before the court on Thursday at 10:00 hours, and warned that the officer in charge of the prison must personally appear before the court and explain any failure to comply with the directive. Zambia Monitor reports that the State acknowledged having contacted the prison authorities but could not explain why the applicants had not been produced.

For the applicants, Milner Katolo told the court that the defence team had worked into the early hours of Wednesday preparing a reply to the State's affidavit, which was served on the lawyers on Tuesday evening. The defence had wanted the applicants in court to sign the documents, he said, but they had not been brought as the court ordered at the previous hearing. For the State, Chief State Advocate Chali Hambayi said the adjournment followed the defence's request for time: the parties had agreed to file by close of business on Tuesday, the State had met that timeline, and the delay came from the other side.

The application itself, as reported by the Times of Zambia on 20 October and News Diggers on 26 October, asks the court to release the 18 unconditionally or on bail on reasonable conditions if they cannot be tried within a reasonable time, and to declare that their continued detention violates their constitutional rights. The applicants argue that they were held for a long time without being brought before a competent court and that the State, by continuing to investigate after charging them, has admitted it is not ready to prosecute. The Times of Zambia reported that the accused face treason and terrorism-related offences; Zambia Monitor's earlier report lists treason, terrorism-related and sedition charges. None of the charges has been tried, and all 18 are presumed innocent.

The case has been adjourned at each sitting since it was first called. On 19 October the State asked for time to respond, the Times of Zambia reported; on 22 October, Zambia Monitor reported, the parties agreed to join the Director of Public Prosecutions, Gilbert Phiri, as a respondent and to drop two officials who had been sued personally, and the court directed that the applicants be produced at the next hearing. They were not.

body.confirmed: The hearing did not start on Wednesday 28 October; the court ordered the 18 applicants produced on Thursday at 10:00 and warned the officer in charge of the prison to appear and explain any failure (Zambia Monitor). The panel is Mulenga, Chibwili and Wishimanga (Zambia Monitor; Times of Zambia). The State filed an affidavit in opposition on Tuesday (Zambia Monitor).

stories.title: Two down and then three up: Zambia's under-15s come back to beat England 3–2 in Baku and reach the last 16 of the first FIFA U-15 World Cup
stories.excerpt: England led 2–0 at the Hovsan complex on Wednesday 28 October before Maxen Msimuko pulled one back before half-time, Samuel Musonda equalised and Chrispine Katoba scored the winner, ZamFoot reports. Brian Kunsanama's side, who finished second in their group on 12 points, now wait to learn their round-of-16 opponent in the tournament's Tier 2 competition.

image.label: Zambia 3 England 2
image.caption: Zambia's under-15 side beat England 3–2 in the round of 32 of the FIFA U-15 World Cup at the Hovsan Competition Complex in Baku on Wednesday 28 October 2026.

body: The Junior Chipolopolo are through to the last 16 of the first FIFA U-15 World Cup, and they got there the hard way. ZamFoot reported on Wednesday 28 October that Zambia beat England 3–2 in a round-of-32 tie in the tournament's Tier 2 competition, played on Pitch 3B of the Hovsan Competition Complex in Baku, after going two goals down.

England scored twice to lead 2–0. Maxen Msimuko of Kafue Celtic, who News Diggers reports scored seven goals in the group stage, pulled one back before half-time. In the second half Samuel Musonda of Sporting Lusaka equalised and Chrispine Katoba, also of Kafue Celtic, scored the winner. ZamFoot's report does not give the minutes of the goals, and the match report on the English FA's website read for this edition covers only the group stage, so the English scorers are not named here.

Brian Kunsanama's squad finished second in their group on 12 points, level with Uruguay but one goal worse off on goal difference, ZamFoot reported on 26 October, after beating Tanzania 3–1, Moldova 2–1, Montserrat 13–0 and Comoros 3–2 and losing 3–1 to Uruguay. Group winners went into Tier A and runners-up into the second tier, which ZamFoot's later report calls Tier 2, in a 180-team festival whose second-tier final is scheduled for Friday 30 October. England, by contrast, had come through Group C with three wins from three: 4–0 against Nicaragua, 2–1 against Montenegro and 10–0 against Cambodia, according to the English FA's own match reports.

The tournament is the first FIFA U-15 World Cup and is being played in Azerbaijan with a festival format that splits teams into tiers after the group stage. Zambia's next opponent in the round of 16 had not been confirmed when ZamFoot published, and no date was given for the tie.

The result adds to a fortnight in which Zambia's youth sides have gone in opposite directions: the Copper Princesses left the U-17 Women's World Cup without a point, as Lusaka Brief reported last week, while the under-15 boys have now won five matches in Baku and eliminated a side that had won all three of its group games.

stories.title: Heroes is open for November: CAF grants the National Heroes Stadium temporary Category 3 approval, bringing the Burundi qualifier to Lusaka on 13 November and the U-23s' tie after
stories.excerpt: A CAF letter dated 28 October, following an inspection from 19 to 22 October, gives the Lusaka stadium temporary approval to host international matches in November, ZamFoot reports. The Chipolopolo's 2027 AFCON qualifier against Burundi moves from Levy Mwanawasa Stadium to Heroes on 13 November, and the under-23s play Burkina Faso there on 15 November, with CAF listing concerns still to be addressed before a further assessment.

image.label: Heroes, 13 November
image.caption: CAF has given the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka temporary Category 3 approval for November 2026, bringing Zambia's AFCON qualifier against Burundi back to the capital.

body: The Chipolopolo will play in Lusaka next month. ZamFoot reported on Thursday 29 October that the Confederation of African Football has granted the National Heroes Stadium temporary Category 3 approval to host international matches in November, in a communication dated 28 October that followed a CAF technical assessment mission at the ground from 19 to 22 October.

Two fixtures move as a result. Zambia's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Burundi on 13 November, which had been set for the Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola, will now be played at Heroes, and the under-23 side's 2028 Olympic Games qualifier against Burkina Faso will follow at the same ground on 15 November.

body.text: We are pleased that CAF has granted National Heroes Stadium temporary Category 3 approval for November.
body.attribution: Charles Chakatazya, FAZ General Secretary, to FAZ Media, as reported by ZamFoot on Thursday 29 October

body: Chakatazya said the assessment confirmed that the stadium met the key requirements for hosting CAF and FIFA matches, thanked the government for the works at the stadium, which he said CAF had acknowledged, and thanked supporters for their patience while the approval was pursued. He urged fans to turn out in numbers for both matches.

The approval is for November only. ZamFoot reports that CAF raised outstanding concerns that must be addressed before a further assessment, without listing them, and that more work is needed to meet the confederation's requirements in full. A longer approval would depend on that next inspection.

The decision brings a home international back to the capital; the Burundi match had been scheduled for Ndola. It comes in a week in which FAZ also said it had bought wireless communication systems, headsets and chargers for match officials in the Super League and National Division One, to be used from Week Six of the league, with Chakatazya saying the purchase fulfilled a promise by FAZ president Keith Mweemba: "The President promised, and he has delivered." For a government that has spent on the ground, the Burundi match is the first test of the facility.

stories.title: A ministry of its own: Christopher Chibuye of Mkushi North becomes the first Minister of Culture and Arts, five years after the arts were folded into Youth and Sport
stories.excerpt: Among the 24 ministers sworn in on Wednesday 28 October is the first head of a stand-alone Ministry of Culture and Arts, created when Parliament dissolved the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts on Tuesday. The Vice-President told the House that culture and arts should be seen as an economic opportunity that can draw tourists and create jobs; the sector's new minister is a Mkushi North MP who came to the UPND from the PF.

image.label: Culture and Arts
image.caption: Zambia's first stand-alone Ministry of Culture and Arts was created by Parliament on Tuesday 27 October 2026 and given its first minister, Christopher Chibuye, the next day.

body: Zambia's artists now have a Cabinet minister whose title names them and nothing else. Christopher Chibuye, the MP for Mkushi North, was sworn in as Minister of Culture and Arts at State House on Wednesday 28 October, Zambia Monitor and Open Zambia reported, as one of 24 ministers appointed to fill the government of 30 ministries that Parliament approved the day before. Open Zambia describes him as a former PF member of Parliament.

The ministry is new. The Zambia Daily Mail's account of Tuesday's motion lists the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts among the five ministries dissolved and Culture and Arts and Youth and Sports among the ten created or reconstituted, and Open Zambia's list of the 30 ministries places Culture and Arts last. Youth and Sports goes to Likando Mufalali, the Senanga MP and UPND national chairperson for elections and campaigns.

Moving the motion, Vice-President Mutale Nalumango argued that culture and arts should be seen as an economic opportunity that can attract tourists and create jobs, the Daily Mail reported. That is the same framing State House gave the whole realignment, which it said would put the machinery of government behind the Grow Zambia Agenda; Open Zambia reported the appendix to the President's request as leaning toward the productive economy.

The change reverses one of the President's own 2021 decisions. Following his election in 2021, the Times of Zambia reported on Tuesday, the President moved the arts portfolio from the Ministry of Tourism to the Ministry of Youth and Sport. The minister who ran that combined portfolio in the first term, Elvis Nkandu, was on Wednesday given Information and Media.

body.text: What the sector will be watching

body: A ministry with its own minister is also a ministry with its own vote in the budget, and the budget is now due on 6 November. The sector will be reading the estimates for the first line that belongs to Culture and Arts alone. Nothing in the published documents says what the new ministry will cost to run or which functions it inherits, and no report read for this edition carried a first statement from the new minister.

Zambia Monitor reported that the President told all his new ministers to work with diligence, integrity and commitment to national unity, and to be confidential, fair, transparent and accountable. For a ministry created on the argument that culture is an economic opportunity, the measure of that argument will be in the estimates.

analysis.title: What the names say: continuity at the centre, new owners for the growth targets
analysis.body: Read as a whole, Wednesday's list is conservative where the state is coercive and experimental where it is productive. Defence, Justice, Home Affairs and Local Government went to first-term ministers moved sideways or returned, and the two nominated MPs sworn in on Tuesday were in Cabinet the next day. The new ministries, by contrast, went to a mix: two former energy ministers split Energy between them, a civil-society policy specialist takes Trade and Exports, an economist from the road fund takes Industry, and a former PF MP takes Culture and Arts. That pattern supports the government's account of the realignment, that each Grow Zambia target now has a named owner, and it also supports the critics' point, that the test is whether owners with new letterheads can deliver what one ministry could not. Two things remain open. The published documents still give no cost, and the first budget these ministers defend is now a week away. And the outlets disagree on who holds Education and who holds Skills and Higher Education, which is the kind of detail a gazette settles; until it is gazetted, the lists are reports.

analysis.title: A budget delayed a week is still a budget written before the Cabinet existed
analysis.body: Moving the reading to 6 November answers the narrowest form of Citizens First's objection: ministers appointed on Wednesday will not be asked to defend estimates on Friday. It does not answer the wider one, that the 2027 budget was built by the Treasury and the four ministers who existed while the other 24 posts were empty, and that the new ministers inherit it rather than shape it. The government's reply, implicit in the sequence of the last week, is that the realignment had to come first precisely so that the estimates could be read against the ministries that will spend them. What the week buys is time to redraw the votes along the new lines, and that is worth watching: thirty ministries need thirty heads of expenditure. The substance is unchanged by the date. ZIPAR wants PAYE left alone and the revenue base widened; the President told his ministers that PAYE alone would lift revenue and that investors could be given incentives; farmers are owed K14.6 billion that the supplementary budget is meant to clear.

analysis.title: Three sittings, no hearing: what the prison's absence does to the bail application
analysis.body: The application before the High Court is about delay: the 18 argue that holding them while the State continues to investigate is itself the violation. Each adjournment therefore does something an ordinary adjournment does not. It extends the detention the applicants say is unlawful, and it adds to the record the court will weigh. Wednesday's order, that the prison produce the 18 at 10:00 and that its officer in charge explain any failure in person, is the court saying so. The State's position is a reasonable one on its face: it filed its affidavit on time and the defence asked for more time to reply. The defence's position is also reasonable: it could not finalise a reply its clients had not signed because the prison did not bring them. What neither side controls is the Correctional Service, and the question the court may now have to decide first is why a directive to produce prisoners was not followed. Whatever the panel rules on bail, the charges of treason, terrorism and sedition remain untried, and the 18 are presumed innocent of all of them. Thursday morning will show whether the hearing finally begins.
